events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.95)
events.body:
The complaint is a rider-filed safety incident alleging that the driver made repeated comments about her body and asked for her number, leaving her feeling harassed and unsafe. That places the case squarely under SAFE-1, which expressly covers "unwanted sexual advances" and harassment/abuse of any kind, and which requires that no automated ruling be issued and the matter be sent to a person [F3][F4][SAFE-1]. The policy execution trace marks the SAFE-1 screen ✓ with "allowed outcomes: escalate", so escalation — which both advocates also request — is the only consistent outcome.

The rider's account rests on her complaint narrative alone: the in-app chat between rider and driver contains no messages at all, before, during or after the trip, so there is no message, timestamp or quoted word from which the alleged remarks can be read in context [F3][SAFE-1]. The driver's only response is a post-trip written statement, "I made small talk. Nothing inappropriate happened.", which is a party statement, not a system record, and therefore cannot be treated as proof of the negative any more than the complaint proves the affirmative [F4][SAFE-1]. Both sides accordingly ask the reviewer, not the automated process, to weigh the words; I record the content question as undetermined and leave it to the human reviewer.

No system record speaks to the interaction at all. The GPS record shows an actual driven distance of 17.1 km against an optimal 17.2 km, i.e. -0.1 km (-0%), with a duration of 25.8 min against 23.6 min estimated — a short, ordinary completed ride with no off-route segment and no anomaly that either corroborates or contradicts the rider's narrative [F1][F2][RD-1]. There is likewise no fare add-on item in dispute: the ride was a fixed-quote RydeX trip of $35.70 with no ERP, waiting, cancellation or other add-on computable from any fare or gps fact, so no monetary remedy under the fare rules arises and the amount is null [F1][F2][FARE-1].

Profiles cannot decide this question. The rider's account (129 days old, rating 4.5, 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days) and the driver's record (327 days, rating 4.67, 999 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes, 0 upheld) are context only; they neither establish nor disprove a SAFE-1 allegation, and no route or no-show ground of complaint exists on any view of them [F5][F6][RD-6][NS-1].

Safety screen: read in full the complaint, the driver's statement and the (empty) chat. The complaint alleges harassment/sexual harassment by the driver (unwanted advances), which is a SAFE-1 category, so safety_concern is recorded as "suspected" and no automated remedy is issued; I found no threat of violence and no accident, injury or dangerous-driving allegation, so SAFE-2 is not engaged [F3][F4][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Evidence status is "insufficient" for any merits finding: the conduct at issue is entirely unrecorded — the chat is empty and the only account of the words is the rider's post-trip complaint plus the driver's post-trip denial — so the record does not settle the elements SAFE-1 needs and only a person can [F3][F4][SAFE-1].

ruling.recommended_action: Refer to a Ryde human reviewer for SAFE-1 handling: no account sanction and no fare adjustment on this record; note no in-app evidence exists either way, and record both parties' clean 90-day dispute histories as context only.

ruling.recommended_action: Refer to a Ryde human reviewer for SAFE-1 handling: no account sanction and no fare adjustment on this record; note no in-app evidence exists either way, and record both parties' clean 90-day dispute histories as context only.
ruling.reasoning:
The complaint is a rider-filed safety incident alleging that the driver made repeated comments about her body and asked for her number, leaving her feeling harassed and unsafe. That places the case squarely under SAFE-1, which expressly covers "unwanted sexual advances" and harassment/abuse of any kind, and which requires that no automated ruling be issued and the matter be sent to a person [F3][F4][SAFE-1]. The policy execution trace marks the SAFE-1 screen ✓ with "allowed outcomes: escalate", so escalation — which both advocates also request — is the only consistent outcome.

The rider's account rests on her complaint narrative alone: the in-app chat between rider and driver contains no messages at all, before, during or after the trip, so there is no message, timestamp or quoted word from which the alleged remarks can be read in context [F3][SAFE-1]. The driver's only response is a post-trip written statement, "I made small talk. Nothing inappropriate happened.", which is a party statement, not a system record, and therefore cannot be treated as proof of the negative any more than the complaint proves the affirmative [F4][SAFE-1]. Both sides accordingly ask the reviewer, not the automated process, to weigh the words; I record the content question as undetermined and leave it to the human reviewer.

No system record speaks to the interaction at all. The GPS record shows an actual driven distance of 17.1 km against an optimal 17.2 km, i.e. -0.1 km (-0%), with a duration of 25.8 min against 23.6 min estimated — a short, ordinary completed ride with no off-route segment and no anomaly that either corroborates or contradicts the rider's narrative [F1][F2][RD-1]. There is likewise no fare add-on item in dispute: the ride was a fixed-quote RydeX trip of $35.70 with no ERP, waiting, cancellation or other add-on computable from any fare or gps fact, so no monetary remedy under the fare rules arises and the amount is null [F1][F2][FARE-1].

Profiles cannot decide this question. The rider's account (129 days old, rating 4.5, 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days) and the driver's record (327 days, rating 4.67, 999 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes, 0 upheld) are context only; they neither establish nor disprove a SAFE-1 allegation, and no route or no-show ground of complaint exists on any view of them [F5][F6][RD-6][NS-1].

Safety screen: read in full the complaint, the driver's statement and the (empty) chat. The complaint alleges harassment/sexual harassment by the driver (unwanted advances), which is a SAFE-1 category, so safety_concern is recorded as "suspected" and no automated remedy is issued; I found no threat of violence and no accident, injury or dangerous-driving allegation, so SAFE-2 is not engaged [F3][F4][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Evidence status is "insufficient" for any merits finding: the conduct at issue is entirely unrecorded — the chat is empty and the only account of the words is the rider's post-trip complaint plus the driver's post-trip denial — so the record does not settle the elements SAFE-1 needs and only a person can [F3][F4][SAFE-1].

rejected_claims.reason: The claim that the harassment allegation 'stands' because no system record contradicts it inverts the rule that missing evidence is never treated as favouring either side [F3][F4][SAFE-1]; the record supports no merits finding for the rider, only escalation, and the rider advocate itself concedes as much in rebuttal to D6/C4.

The claim that the rider's clean profile in some way supports her account is a profile fact deciding a safety question, which is barred: profiles never decide a case alone and do not bear on the truth of the allegation [F5][F6][SAFE-1]; the rider advocate concedes C4 is overstated.

The claim that the driver's clean profile (327 days, 999 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes) supports imposing no account sanction is a profile fact used to decide the case: profile facts may only support an added action and can never ground or defeat a finding [F6][RD-6]; it is rejected as a merits argument although the separate RD-6 predicate (no upheld route dispute in 90 days) is in any event unmet [F6][RD-6].

The part of D3 that would place this case outside the sexual-harassment category is rejected: SAFE-1 expressly covers harassment and unwanted sexual advances, which is what the complaint alleges, and I so found; D3's operative conclusion (route to a person under SAFE-1, not SAFE-2) is accepted [F3][F4][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

Accepted as far as it goes — no off-route segment or route-deviation ground exists — but it does not dispose of the case, because the live SAFE-1 allegation is unaffected by the route being clean [F1][F2][RD-1][SAFE-1]; the same applies to D5, which correctly shows no monetary remedy is computable [F1][F2][FARE-1].

claims.assertion: The rider's complaint states that the driver repeatedly commented on her body and asked for her number, and that she felt harassed and unsafe — an allegation of harassment/sexual harassment of a passenger during the trip.

The chat record contains no in-app messages before, during or after the trip, so the driver's conduct was never denied or addressed in any contemporaneous in-app exchange; the only denial is the driver's own post-trip written statement 'I made small talk. Nothing inappropriate happened.' (F4), which is a self-serving statement, not a system record.

No system record (GPS, timeline or fare) contradicts the rider's account of the interaction — the trip is a completed 17.1 km / 25.8 min ride (F1, F2) and no record speaks to the driver's words either way, so the harassment allegation stands for human assessment on the rider's complaint alone.

The rider's account is the account of a 129-day-old account with rating 4.5 and zero prior disputes in 90 days (F5); the driver has 999 trips in 90 days and 0 disputes (F6); neither profile decides the safety question, which must go to a person.

The route itself is not in dispute: the driver covered 17.1 km against a 17.2 km optimal route (-0.1 km, -0%) with duration 25.8 min vs 23.6 min (F1, F2), so no route-deviation or fare issue arises and the only remaining question is the safety allegation.

weaknesses: The rider produced no message evidence: the chat record is empty (F3), so the harassment claim rests on her complaint narrative alone with no in-app corroboration.

The driver denies the allegation in a written statement (F4), and the rider did not report any off-platform message, so the record contains no objective corroboration of the body comments or the request for her number.

There is no request for a monetary refund: the fare facts are empty for this dispute type and no additional fee is identifiable from F1/F2, so the outcome sought is escalation and account review rather than a refund.

The rider's profile (F5) and the driver's otherwise clean 999-trip, 0-dispute history (F6) give the human reviewer no prior pattern to lean on for either side; F6 could be read against the rider's account, though a good record cannot disprove an incident and the rider has 0 disputes in 90 d.

claims.assertion: The rider's complaint is a harassment allegation about the driver's remarks and a request for her number; a body-comment/harassment allegation is a SAFE-1 matter, and SAFE-1 requires escalation to a human reviewer rather than any automated fare ruling, so the driver does not oppose an escalate outcome.

The in-app chat record contains no messages at all between rider and driver (F3), so the rider's account of the remarks rests on her post-trip complaint only; the driver's contemporaneous position is recorded in his statement that he 'made small talk' and that nothing inappropriate happened (F4); there is thus no message, timestamp or quoted word in the record from which the content of the alleged remarks can be checked.

The complaint and the file contain no threat, intimidation, unwanted sexual advance, or dangerous-driving incident recorded in a system fact and no accident or injury is alleged, so classifying the case under SAFE-2's accident/dangerous-driving route would be unsupported; the appropriate route is SAFE-1 referral to a person.

The GPS record shows the actual driven distance was 17.1 km against an optimal 17.2 km (-0.1 km, -0%) (F1) with a duration of 25.8 min versus 23.6 min estimated (F2), so there is no off-route segment and no route-deviation ground of complaint against the driver; nothing in this case supports a fare deduction.

The service was a fixed-quote RydeX trip charged $35.70, and no ERP, waiting, cancellation or other add-on item is in dispute, so no monetary remedy under the fare rules can be computed from any fare or gps fact in this record.

The driver's profile shows 327 days of account history, a 4.67 rating over 999 trips in 90 days and 0 disputes and 0 upheld complaints (route: 0, no-show: 0) (F6), which is consistent with a driver with no prior conduct record and supports not imposing any account sanction on him for this single, uncorroborated allegation.

weaknesses: The chat record is empty (F3), so the driver's own written account is the only thing on his side; a judge may read the absence of any in-app record as leaving the rider's account of the remarks standing, and my client cannot point to a single message or timestamp that contradicts her.

The rider also has a clean profile (129-day account, 4.5 rating, 0 disputes in 90 days, 0 upheld) (F5), so there is no credibility record on the rider side for me to attack, and the judge may give her complaint weight on that basis.

SAFE-1 itself says the semantic question of whether remarks amount to harassment is for the tribunal reading the words, not for the code; because the words are unrecorded, I cannot show they were innocuous, and the case is likely to go to a person regardless of my client's denial (F3, F4).

points.response: Agreed that the harassment allegation is a SAFE-1 matter requiring escalation to a person, not an automated ruling — that is exactly the outcome I ask for, so this point is conceded as to the remedy and not as to the merits of the rider's account.

The empty chat record (F3) means the remarks are unrecorded, not that they did not occur; under SAFE-1 the semantic question of whether the remarks amount to harassment is for the tribunal reading the record, and the driver's own post-trip denial (F4) is a statement, not a system record, so it cannot defeat the rider's account.

I do not rely on SAFE-2: no accident, injury or dangerous-driving incident is in the record, so the case is correctly routed under SAFE-1; note however that SAFE-1 expressly covers 'Unwanted Sexual Advances' and threats/intimidation, which is precisely what the rider's complaint alleges (F3).

Conceded: the GPS record shows 17.1 km actual against 17.2 km optimal (-0.1 km, -0%) (F1) with 25.8 min against 23.6 min estimated (F2), so there is no off-route segment and I make no route-deviation or fare claim.
Conceded: no fare fact exists for this dispute type and no add-on item is computable from F1/F2, so no monetary remedy is sought and my ask remains escalation only.

The driver's clean profile (F6) is a profile fact that cannot decide a SAFE-1 allegation and does not bear on whether the rider's account is true; a long, uneventful trip history is also consistent with an incident that simply was never reported before, and the rider is equally clean (F5).

I note my own claim C4 is overstated: profiles (F5, F6) cannot decide the safety question, and the human reviewer should weigh the rider's complaint on its own terms rather than on either party's rating record.

The words of the complaint are the rider's own narrative and no in-app message exists to embody them (F3); under SAFE-1 the meaning of unrecorded remarks is for a human to read, and my client neither admits nor can be found liable for any automated consequence on this record — I do not contest that the allegation must be screened as a safety matter, and my own brief already asked for escalate.

The rider is right that the driver's statement (F4) is a party statement, not a system record, and that the chat is empty (F3); that cuts both ways — there is equally no system record of any improper remark, so the rider's narrative is likewise uncorroborated, and the judge should record the question as undetermined and send it to a person rather than treat either party's words as proven.

I accept that no system record speaks to the driver's words (F1, F2, F3), but the same absence means no system record supports the rider's account either; the completed 17.1 km ride with no off-route segment (F1) and normal 25.8 min duration (F2) shows the trip itself was carried out per the booking and gives the reviewer no conduct evidence in either direction.

I agree the profiles do not decide the safety question; I only ask that the reviewer note that my client's 327-day account with 999 trips and 0 disputes in 90 days (F6) shows no prior pattern and therefore no basis for any account sanction, which profile facts may support but never establish on their own.

Agreed — the GPS record shows 17.1 km against an optimal 17.2 km (-0.1 km, -0%) (F1) and 25.8 min against 23.6 min estimated (F2), so there is no off-route segment, no route-deviation finding and no fare adjustment; the only live question is the safety allegation, which goes to a person.
